1 mark: Connect a driver cell across the uniform potentiometer wire; connect each test cell in turn via a galvanometer and jockey
1 mark: Find the balance lengths l1 and l2 where the galvanometer shows no deflection
1 mark: E1/E2 = l1/l2
questions.explanation: (a) E.m.f. is the open-circuit p.d.; terminal p.d. is the p.d. while current flows (E - Ir). (b)(i) 4.5 ohms. (ii) 1.8 A. (iii) 8.1 V. (iv) 3.6^2/3 = 4.32 W. (c) Find balance lengths for each cell; E1/E2 = l1/l2.

questions.stem:
(a) State Faraday's law and Lenz's law of electromagnetic induction. [4 marks]
(b) Explain why a transformer does not work with a steady direct current. [2 marks]
(c) A transformer with 1 200 turns in its primary coil and 60 turns in its secondary coil is connected to a 240 V a.c. mains supply. Its input power is 600 W and its efficiency is 90%. Calculate:
(i) the secondary voltage; [2 marks]
(ii) the output power; [2 marks]
(iii) the secondary current. [2 marks]
(d) State three ways of reducing energy losses in a transformer. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Faraday: the magnitude of the induced e.m.f. is directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage
2 marks: Lenz: the induced current flows in such a direction as to oppose the change producing it
1 mark: A steady d.c. produces a constant magnetic flux in the core
1 mark: There is no change of flux linking the secondary, so no e.m.f. is induced
1 mark: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np, Vs = 240 x 60/1200
1 mark: Vs = 12 V
1 mark: Output power = 0.90 x 600
1 mark: = 540 W
1 mark: Is = Ps/Vs = 540/12
1 mark: Is = 45 A
3 marks: Any three, 1 mark each: laminated core (eddy currents); thick low-resistance copper windings (I^2R losses); soft iron core (hysteresis loss); good core design so all flux links both coils (flux leakage)
questions.explanation: (a) Induced e.m.f. is proportional to the rate of change of flux linkage; induced current opposes its cause. (b) Steady d.c. gives no changing flux. (c)(i) 12 V. (ii) 540 W. (iii) 45 A. (d) Laminated soft-iron core, thick copper wire, well-linked coils.

questions.topic: Series circuit containing resistor, inductor and capacitor
questions.stem:
(a) Define (i) reactance; (ii) impedance. [2 marks]
(b) A 40 ohm resistor, a 0.5 H inductor of negligible resistance and a 20 microfarad capacitor are connected in series to a 100 V (r.m.s.), 50 Hz supply. Taking pi = 3.142, calculate:
(i) the inductive reactance; [2 marks]
(ii) the capacitive reactance; [2 marks]
(iii) the impedance of the circuit; [2 marks]
(iv) the r.m.s. current. [2 marks]
(c) Calculate the resonant frequency of the circuit and comment on your answer in relation to the supply frequency. [3 marks]
(d) State two applications of resonance in a.c. circuits. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Reactance: the opposition to a.c. offered by an inductor or a capacitor
1 mark: Impedance: the total (effective) opposition to a.c. in a circuit containing resistance and reactance
1 mark: X_L = 2 pi f L = 2 x 3.142 x 50 x 0.5
1 mark: = 157.1 ohms
1 mark: X_C = 1/(2 pi f C) = 1/(2 x 3.142 x 50 x 20 x 10^-6)
1 mark: = 159.2 ohms
1 mark: Z = sqrt(R^2 + (X_C - X_L)^2) = sqrt(40^2 + 2.1^2)
1 mark: Z = 40.1 ohms
1 mark: I = V/Z = 100/40.1
1 mark: I = 2.5 A
1 mark: f0 = 1/(2 pi sqrt(LC)) = 1/(2 x 3.142 x sqrt(0.5 x 20 x 10^-6))
1 mark: f0 = 50.3 Hz
1 mark: This is very close to the supply frequency, so the circuit is almost at resonance and Z is nearly equal to R
2 marks: Any two, 1 mark each: tuning circuits of radio and television receivers; selecting frequencies in filters/oscillators; transmitters
questions.explanation: (a) Reactance is opposition to a.c. from L or C; impedance is the total opposition. (b)(i) 157.1 ohms. (ii) 159.2 ohms. (iii) 40.1 ohms. (iv) 2.5 A. (c) f0 = 50.3 Hz, almost equal to 50 Hz, so the circuit is near resonance. (d) Radio tuning, filters.

questions.stem:
(a) What is meant by the photoelectric effect? [2 marks]
(b) State two observations of the photoelectric effect that cannot be explained by the wave theory of light. [2 marks]
(c) Light of wavelength 4.0 x 10^-7 m falls on a metal surface whose work function is 2.2 eV. Calculate:
(i) the energy of each photon; [2 marks]
(ii) the threshold frequency of the metal; [2 marks]
(iii) the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons; [2 marks]
(iv) the stopping potential. [2 marks]
(h = 6.6 x 10^-34 J s; c = 3.0 x 10^8 m/s; 1 eV = 1.6 x 10^-19 J)
(d) State three applications of photocells. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: The emission of electrons from a metal surface when electromagnetic radiation of sufficiently high frequency falls on it
2 marks: Any two, 1 mark each: no emission below the threshold frequency however intense the light; maximum KE depends on frequency not intensity; emission is instantaneous
1 mark: E = hc/lambda = 6.6 x 10^-34 x 3.0 x 10^8/4.0 x 10^-7
1 mark: E = 4.95 x 10^-19 J
1 mark: W = 2.2 x 1.6 x 10^-19 = 3.52 x 10^-19 J; f0 = W/h
1 mark: f0 = 5.33 x 10^14 Hz
1 mark: KEmax = hf - W = 4.95 x 10^-19 - 3.52 x 10^-19
1 mark: = 1.43 x 10^-19 J
1 mark: eVs = KEmax, Vs = 1.43 x 10^-19/1.6 x 10^-19
1 mark: Vs = 0.89 V
3 marks: Any three, 1 mark each: automatic doors; burglar alarms; light meters in cameras; solar calculators/solar panels; counting objects on conveyor belts; sound track reproduction in films
questions.explanation: (a) Emission of electrons from a metal by light of high enough frequency. (b) Threshold frequency exists; KEmax depends on frequency only. (c)(i) 4.95 x 10^-19 J. (ii) 5.33 x 10^14 Hz. (iii) 1.43 x 10^-19 J. (iv) 0.89 V. (d) Automatic doors, burglar alarms, light meters.

questions.stem:
(a) What is meant by (i) radioactivity; (ii) half-life? [4 marks]
(b) Copy and complete a table comparing alpha particles, beta particles and gamma rays under the headings: nature, charge, penetrating power. [3 marks]
(c) A radioactive source used in a hospital has a half-life of 6 hours. If its initial activity is 160 counts per second, calculate its activity after 24 hours. [3 marks]
(d) In a fusion reaction the mass defect is 0.0304 u. Calculate the energy released in joules. (1 u = 1.66 x 10^-27 kg; c = 3.0 x 10^8 m/s) [3 marks]
(e) State two safety precautions in handling radioactive sources. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Radioactivity: the spontaneous disintegration of unstable nuclei with emission of alpha, beta or gamma radiation
2 marks: Half-life: the time taken for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay (or for the activity to fall to half)
1 mark: Alpha: helium nucleus, charge +2e, low penetration (stopped by paper)
1 mark: Beta: fast electron, charge -e, moderate penetration (stopped by a few mm of aluminium)
1 mark: Gamma: electromagnetic radiation, no charge, very high penetration (reduced by thick lead/concrete)
1 mark: 24 hours = 4 half-lives
1 mark: Activity = 160 x (1/2)^4
1 mark: = 10 counts per second
1 mark: Mass defect = 0.0304 x 1.66 x 10^-27 = 5.05 x 10^-29 kg
1 mark: E = mc^2 = 5.05 x 10^-29 x 9 x 10^16
1 mark: E = 4.54 x 10^-12 J

questions.stem:
(a) State the principle of moments. [2 marks]
(b) State the two conditions necessary for a rigid body to be in equilibrium under the action of parallel forces. [2 marks]
(c) A uniform plank AB, 6 m long and weighing 400 N, rests horizontally on two supports P and Q placed 1 m from A and 1 m from B respectively. A boy weighing 900 N stands on the plank 2 m from A. Calculate:
(i) the reaction at Q; [3 marks]
(ii) the reaction at P. [2 marks]
(d) The boy now walks towards B. How far beyond Q can he go before the plank begins to tip? [4 marks]
(e) State two ways of increasing the stability of a body. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: For a body in equilibrium, the sum of the clockwise moments about any point equals the sum of the anticlockwise moments about the same point
1 mark: The resultant force (sum of upward forces = sum of downward forces) is zero
1 mark: The sum of the moments about any point is zero
1 mark: Take moments about P: plank weight acts 2 m from P, boy 1 m from P, Q is 4 m from P
1 mark: R_Q x 4 = 900 x 1 + 400 x 2
1 mark: R_Q = 425 N
1 mark: R_P + R_Q = 900 + 400
1 mark: R_P = 875 N
1 mark: Plank is about to tip about Q when R_P = 0
1 mark: Take moments about Q: 900 x d = 400 x 2 (centre of plank is 2 m from Q)
1 mark: d = 800/900
1 mark: d = 0.89 m beyond Q (before reaching end B, which is 1 m beyond Q)
